title: Continue to handle notifications even when Notifications tray icon is disabled
line: Notifications keep working without a Notifications widget, for example after removing the System Tray or the panel it was in.
explanation: The notification server and the popups lived in the Notifications widget's shared state, which only existed while a Notifications widget was loaded, and popups could only be placed next to such a widget. Without one (no System Tray, tray or panel removed, custom layouts) nobody owned org.freedesktop.Notifications and every notification was lost. The popups, do-not-disturb handling, global shortcuts and the shared delegates now live in a new module, org.kde.plasma.private.notifications, which plasmashell creates at startup; the widget only shows history and settings and still decides placement when present. Without a widget, popups follow a panel on the primary screen (or its desktop) and move with it, unless the user turned the Notifications entry off in the System Tray to use another notification server.

commits.message:
notifications: show popups from plasmashell instead of the widget

Notifications were only handled while a Notifications widget existed, so
without one they were lost. plasmashell now shows them from a shared
module and the widget only shows history, unless the tray entry is off.

BUG: 485383

+/*

+    SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only OR GPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-KDE-Accepted-GPL

+
+#include "focusedplasmadialog.h"
+
+#include <QGuiApplication>
+
+#include <PlasmaQuick/Dialog>
+#include <PlasmaQuick/PlasmaWindow>
+
+FocusedPlasmaDialog::FocusedPlasmaDialog(QObject *parent)
+    : QObject(parent)
+{
+    connect(qApp, &QGuiApplication::focusWindowChanged, this, &FocusedPlasmaDialog::windowChanged);
+}
+
+static bool isPlasmaWindow(QWindow *window)
+{
+    if (qobject_cast<PlasmaQuick::Dialog *>(window) || qobject_cast<PlasmaQuick::PlasmaWindow *>(window)) {
+        return true;
+    }
+    return false;
+}
+
+QWindow *FocusedPlasmaDialog::window() const
+{
+    auto *focusWindow = qApp->focusWindow();
+    if (isPlasmaWindow(focusWindow)) {
+        return focusWindow;
+    }
+
+    if (focusWindow) {
+        if (isPlasmaWindow(focusWindow->transientParent())) {
+            return focusWindow->transientParent();
+        }
+    }
+
+    return nullptr;
+}
+
+#include "moc_focusedplasmadialog.cpp"

+    // which only shows their history. Only Plasma Desktop uses it, other shells have their own.
+    if (m_notifications || m_shell != u"org.kde.plasma.desktop" || notificationsDisabledInSystemTray()) {
+        return;
+    }
+
+    m_notifications = PlasmaQuick::globalEngine()->singletonInstance<QObject *>("org.kde.plasma.private.notifications", "Globals");
+    if (!m_notifications) {
+        qCWarning(PLASMASHELL) << "Could not load the notifications service";
+        return;
+    }
+
+    connect(this, &Plasma::Corona::availableScreenRectChanged, this, &ShellCorona::updateNotificationsContainment);
+    connect(m_screenPool, &ScreenPool::screenOrderChanged, this, &ShellCorona::updateNotificationsContainment);
+    connect(m_activityController, &KActivities::Controller::currentActivityChanged, this, &ShellCorona::updateNotificationsContainment);
+    updateNotificationsContainment();
+}
+
+bool ShellCorona::notificationsDisabledInSystemTray() const
+{
+    // Turning off the Notifications entry of the System Tray is how notifications are left to
+    // another notification server, unless there is a Notifications widget elsewhere
+    const QString notifications = u"org.kde.plasma.notifications"_s;
+    bool disabled = false;
+
+    const KConfigGroup containments(config(), u"Containments"_s);
+    for (const QString &containmentId : containments.groupList()) {
+        const KConfigGroup applets = containments.group(containmentId).group(u"Applets"_s);
+        for (const QString &appletId : applets.groupList()) {
+            const KConfigGroup applet = applets.group(appletId);
+            if (applet.readEntry("plugin", QString()) == notifications) {
+                return false;
+            }
+
+            // A System Tray keeps its entries in its applet's group
+            const KConfigGroup trayGeneral = applet.group(u"General"_s);
+            if (trayGeneral.readEntry("extraItems", QStringList()).contains(notifications)) {
+                return false;
+            }
+            if (trayGeneral.readEntry("knownItems", QStringList()).contains(notifications)) {
+                disabled = true;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    return disabled;
+}
+
+void ShellCorona::updateNotificationsContainment()
+{
+    // Without a Notifications widget to follow, popups follow a panel on the primary screen,
+    // preferring the bottom, top, right and then left one, or else its desktop
+    const auto score = [](Plasma::Types::Location location) {
+        switch (location) {
+        case Plasma::Types::BottomEdge:
+            return 4;
+        case Plasma::Types::TopEdge:
+            return 3;
+        case Plasma::Types::RightEdge:
+            return 2;
+        case Plasma::Types::LeftEdge:
+            return 1;
+        default:
+            return 0;
+        }
+    };
+
+    Plasma::Containment *containment = nullptr;
+    const auto containments = this->containments();
+    for (Plasma::Containment *candidate : containments) {
+        if (candidate->containmentType() != Plasma::Containment::Panel || candidate->screen() != 0 || candidate->destroyed()) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (!containment || score(candidate->location()) > score(containment->location())) {
+            containment = candidate;
+        }
+    }
+
+    if (!containment) {
+        containment = containmentForScreen(0, m_activityController->currentActivity(), QString());
+    }
+    if (containment) {
+        const auto connection = static_cast<Qt::ConnectionType>(Qt::QueuedConnection | Qt::UniqueConnection);
+        connect(containment, &Plasma::Applet::destroyedChanged, this, &ShellCorona::updateNotificationsContainment, connection);
+        connect(containment, &QObject::destroyed, this, &ShellCorona::updateNotificationsContainment, connection);
+    }
+
+    m_notifications->setProperty("fallbackContainment", QVariant::fromValue<QObject *>(containment));
 }

media.caption: Pure master, System Tray removed and plasmashell restarted: nobody owns org.freedesktop.Notifications, three Notify calls fail and nothing appears
With the fix, same setup: plasmashell owns the name and the three notifications stack above the panel
Still no widget: with the panel at the top popups go top-right, with it on the left they go bottom-left next to it
Two screens, no widget: popups are on the primary screen, and move to the other screen when it becomes primary
Notifications entry turned off in the System Tray and plasmashell restarted: plasmashell leaves the name free and another notification server (xfce4-notifyd here) shows it, as the tray's warning says
No widget: the Do Not Disturb and Clear Notification History global shortcuts still work

review.text: Moving the notification server and popups out of the widget into a shell-owned module is the right direction for this bug, and the testing is thorough. But the opt-out is implemented by ShellCorona parsing the System Tray's private layout config (knownItems/extraItems) once at load, which couples the shell to the tray's config format and stops working live: turning the tray entry off at runtime no longer frees org.freedesktop.Notifications until plasmashell restarts, unlike master. With a 52-file restructuring this also needs Kai's agreement before an MR.
changes: Replace notificationsDisabledInSystemTray() with an explicit setting owned by the notifications stack (e.g. a 'Use Plasma notifications' option in libnotificationmanager's settings / the Notifications KCM), and have the module take or release org.freedesktop.Notifications live when it changes.
If the tray entry is kept as the opt-out, at least react to it at runtime (via the tray applet's config/extraItems change) instead of reading the layout config once at startup.
Agree the design with the notifications maintainer (Kai Uwe Broulik) before opening the MR, given the size of the move.
